name: @radicle-co/infra-shared
description: Shared CDK constructs and pure resolvers for the KitchenSink platform: ALB listener-priority allocation, message-table naming, and the advisory cdk-nag security layer.
//: ⛔ DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THE npm WORKSPACE, and it must stay outside. It sits at `shared/infra` rather
than `packages/shared/infra` for exactly that reason — the root globs include `packages/shared/*`, so
the obvious location would silently make this a workspace again and undo the seam.
WHY IT EXISTS. CDK is not part of the workspace installs. A service's CDK app installs its own
`aws-cdk-lib` inside its `infra/` directory, so `aws-cdk-lib` never enters the root tree and never
reaches `turbo prune`, and therefore never ships inside a service's container image — it was 149 MB of
one.
That only works if the shared constructs resolve the CONSUMER's copy of aws-cdk-lib rather than one of
their own. Two instances is not a packaging nuisance: `SecretValue` tokens minted by one instance are
not resolvable by a stack from the other, and TypeScript rejects the assignment outright ('Types have
separate declarations of a private property'). Hence peerDependencies below — this package owns no CDK
copy and defers instance ownership to whoever installs it. `cdk-nag` is a real dependency because it is
ours to pin, and it peers on aws-cdk-lib itself, so it resolves the same single instance.
⚠️ PUBLISHED TO GITHUB PACKAGES, and that is why this one package breaks the `@kitchensink/*`
naming convention CODING_STANDARDS §406 documents. GitHub Packages requires the npm scope to match
the repository owner, so `@radicle-co` is not a preference — it is the only name the registry will
accept for `radicle-co/KitchenSink`. Every other platform package stays `@kitchensink/*`.
⚠️ Consumers need a token to READ this, because GitHub Packages authenticates even public
packages. CI uses the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`; a local `npm ci` in an `infra/` directory needs a
PAT with `read:packages` in `~/.npmrc`. The trade was accepted deliberately: the alternative was
the public npm registry, which needs no auth but also no longer matched what this repo wanted.
⚠️ Subpath exports keep the three original boundaries (`/alb`, `/messaging`, `/security`) rather than
flattening them into one namespace. They were three packages for a reason and merging the surface would
lose it; only the publishing unit is shared.
⚠️ It declares NEITHER zod NOR dotenv, and must not. Neither is imported here — they were added by
mistake, copied from a consuming CDK app. A dependency this package does not use is not merely
dead weight: it is COPIED into every consumer that installs from the registry, giving them a
second instance of a library the workspace already provides. That split zod and broke
infra-global's typecheck.

⛔ It declares NO `@kitchensink/*` tooling, and must not, even though `eslint.config.js` imports `@kitchensink/eslint`. This package sits outside the npm workspace, so DECLARING one makes npm resolve it from the registry — where a private workspace package does not exist — and `npm install` here fails. Undeclared, Node's upward walk finds the workspace symlink in the repo root's `node_modules`, which the root install has already created by the time `cdk-checks` runs. `packages/infra/global` resolves its own the same way, for the same reason.
